suggestions.rationale: Persistent sexual dysfunction, including erectile dysfunction in men, has been reported after surgically treated cauda equina syndrome in cohorts largely involving lumbar disc herniation. This supports a clinically relevant CES/erectile-dysfunction research pathway when the individual has a compatible CES etiology, documented sacral neurologic involvement, and compatible chronology. These population-level postoperative data do not by themselves establish an individual causal nexus, should not be generalized automatically to every CES etiology, and do not exclude vascular, endocrine, medication-related, psychogenic, or other contributors.
evidenceGaps: Clinical documentation confirming erectile dysfunction and its onset, persistence, and severity

Records establishing the cauda equina syndrome diagnosis, underlying etiology (including whether due to lumbar disc herniation), neurologic level and severity, and relevant sacral findings such as bladder, bowel, perianal sensory, or other sacral nerve-root dysfunction
Pre-CES sexual-function history and chronology comparing CES onset or decompression with erectile-dysfunction onset or worsening
Evaluation of competing erectile-dysfunction contributors, including vascular disease, diabetes, endocrine disorders, medications, psychiatric factors, and other neurologic disease

Urology, neurology, spine, or other qualified medical opinion addressing whether the individual erectile dysfunction is medically attributable to or aggravated by the documented CES rather than an alternative cause

sourceReferences.citation: Moradi et al., BMC Musculoskeletal Disorders (2025), PMID 40380123
sourceReferences.note: Systematic review of 20 studies focused on surgically treated lumbar disc herniation/CES populations; persistent sexual dysfunction was common after CES and erectile dysfunction was the most frequently reported male sexual disorder. Supports this bounded postoperative population, not unrestricted generalization across all CES etiologies or automatic individual causation.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 40380123; abstract/methods/results: 20 eligible studies from 2014-2024; lumbar disc herniation/CES surgical populations; male erectile dysfunction reported at 14%-100%; long-term CES sexual issues 14%-100%; only 1 of 14 CES studies reported postoperative improvement
